translate.label: Translate

explain.label: Explain

extractTables.label: Extract tables
extractTables.prompt: Extract the structured data on this page (prices, plans, specs, lists) as Markdown tables.

research.label: Research
research.prompt:
Research this: search several sources, read about eight of the most relevant pages, and compare them in a table with sources.

Question:

prices.label: Compare prices
prices.prompt: Compare prices for this product: find the same model at other stores and compare what I would pay delivered (price, shipping, taxes and fees, coupons). Give a table with store, price, shipping, total, stock and link, and say which offer is best.

reviews.label: Reviews
reviews.description: What buyers praise and complain about
reviews.prompt: Summarize this product's reviews: the rating and how many reviews there are, what people like, and the problems several reviewers describe (quote one for each). Read past the first page: the most recent and the lowest-rated reviews. Say if any look fake.

flaws.label: Watch-outs
flaws.prompt: Before I buy this, what should I watch out for? Check who sells and ships it, returns and warranty, extra costs (shipping, taxes, subscriptions), the specs, common faults in the low-rated reviews, and whether the discount is real. List only what matters.

deal.label: Good deal?
deal.prompt: Is this price a good deal? Check whether the discount is real (the price over the last months, the price at other stores), compare with similar products, and tell me: buy now, wait, or skip, and why.

reputation.label: Reputation
reputation.prompt: What do people say about this product? Look at reviewers' tests and at what owners report on forums and social media. Tell me what they like and what they complain about, with links to the sources.

trust.label: Can I trust this shop?
trust.prompt: Can I trust this shop? Check the site and the seller: its address, its contact and return details, how it takes payment, and what others report about it. Tell me how sure you are.

sites.title: Site access
sites.description: Sites and API hosts this extension may use. Each is asked for on first use.
sites.policiesDescription: What the agent may do on a site. A rule for example.com covers its subdomains.
sites.defaultPolicy: Other sites follow the mode in the side panel. The stricter of rule and mode wins, except that Automatic sites skip Manual approval. High-risk steps always ask.

social.title: Forums and social media
social.description: Here the assistant only reads, in the tab, signed in as you. A like, a vote, a follow or a post always asks you first. A site on the list covers its subdomains.
social.pages: Pages of one such site a request looks at
social.none: No sites: these rules apply nowhere.

language.title: Language
language.description: Interface language. Replies follow the language you write in.

region.title: Country or region
region.hint: For prices, shops, delivery and buying advice; the model is told it with each request. With Automatic, the extension asks api.country.is (or Cloudflare, when that does not answer) for the country of your IP address, at most every 12 hours. That service sees your IP address. Choose a country, or not to tell the model, and nothing is looked up.
region.notFound: The country of your IP address is not known: the model is not told one.

data.exportHint: Settings and conversations in one file.
data.encryptHint: AES-256. The password isn't saved: lose it and the file can't be opened.
data.includeKeysHint: Encrypted with the rest of the file.
data.keysNeedPassword: Keys are exported only in an encrypted file.
data.importHint: Replaces your settings and adds the file's conversations.

data.wrongPassword: Wrong password, or the file is damaged.

data.importConfirm_other: Replace your settings and add {{count}} conversations?
data.clearHint: Messages, attached pages and task records. Settings stay.
data.clearConfirm: Delete every conversation? This can't be undone.
data.resetHint: Conversations, settings, API keys, site rules and site access.
data.resetConfirm: Erase all conversations, settings and API keys? This can't be undone.

about.title: About
about.updateSteps: Run this again, then click reload on the extension's card at chrome://extensions. Your data stays.
about.autoCheckHint: Asks GitHub for the latest version. Nothing about you is sent.
about.privacy: No Browser Helper server. Conversations stay in this browser; requests go straight to your providers.
about.keys: API keys stay in the extension's storage. Web pages can't read them.

reason.payment: Looks like a payment or purchase.
reason.destructive: Looks hard to undo: a deletion, cancellation or account change.
reason.confirmEach: Your rule for this site asks every time.
reason.injection: This page tried to instruct the assistant, so it now asks before changes and new sites.
reason.exfiltration: The address contains data (an email, a card number, a long code). Send it to this site?
reason.newSite: This site hasn't come up in this task.
reason.secret: The text looks like a key or token. Enter it on this site?
reason.clipboard: Pastes your clipboard into the page. The assistant can't see what's on it.
reason.frame: Acts inside another site's frame, which the assistant can't read.
reason.download: Downloads a file. Only allow files you expect.
reason.sensitivePage: This page handles account security, keys or payments, so every change asks.
reason.unseen: The assistant can't read what is drawn here. Check the picture.
reason.watch: The page is read again, in the background, without touching it, for up to 30 days. Your model is asked only when what it watches on the page changes.
reason.social: This acts in your name on a social site (a like, a follow, a post).

agentSettings.title: Agent
agentSettings.description: How the assistant works on web pages.
agentSettings.useCdpHint: More reliable. Chrome shows a debugging bar while a task runs.
agentSettings.cdpUnavailable: Not in this build (no debugger permission).
agentSettings.notifications: Notify me when a task needs me
agentSettings.maxStepsHint: {{min}} to {{max}}; {{usual}} unless you change it. A task that goes in circles uses more of your model's tokens with a higher limit.
agentSettings.modeHint: Also switchable below the message box, even mid-task.
agentSettings.reasoningEffortHint: Controls how long reasoning models think. Auto stays fast on routine browser steps and helper calls; switchable below the message box even mid-task.
agentSettings.screenshotsHint: Auto: the current model if it reads images, else the vision model.
agentSettings.visionStrategy: When to look at the screen
agentSettings.visionStrategyHint: DOM stays primary for accuracy and safety. Auto adds a screenshot on canvas/icon pages or when an action had no effect; Always adds a compact numbered screenshot to every view with a multimodal model. Never on sign-in, account or payment pages.
agentSettings.recordStepsHint: A small screenshot before each step, stored on this device. Not on sign-in, account or payment pages.

commands.hint: When a task has finished, save it as a command and run it again by typing its name after a slash.

voice.micGranted: Browser Helper may use the microphone.

voice.conversationHint: After a spoken question, the microphone reopens once the reply has been read.

deepseek.title: DeepSeek Search API

search.engineFallbackHint: Used when the API fails, if allowed below.

watch.title: Watched pages
watch.empty: Ask the assistant to tell you when something happens on a page, e.g. “tell me when this drops below $20”.
watch.footnote: A watched page is opened in the background and only read. Your model is asked when what is watched changes, not at every look. A page is reloaded at most every 30 seconds, unless you rush it.

notification.failed: {{site}} could not be checked several times in a row: {{condition}}

watch.liveHint: At this pace the page stays open in a collapsed tab group, and is reloaded every 30 seconds.

rush.confirm: For the next {{minutes}} minutes this page is reloaded every {{seconds}} seconds. The site may answer with a CAPTCHA or block you. Start?

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: How the assistant goes about a kind of work, and what its answer looks like. It loads a skill when the work comes up.
skills.builtinHint: Come with the extension. Turn off the ones you do not want.
skills.installedHint: Skills you wrote or installed. Type a slash and the name to use one.

add.addressPlaceholder: https://github.com/…/skills/name, or the address of a SKILL.md or a zip
add.formats: A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md, in the Agent Skills format. Choose its SKILL.md or a zip of the folder, or give the address of the folder on GitHub.

form.note: A skill is instructions the assistant follows as if they were yours. Install only what you have read. It is text, not code, and cannot turn off approvals.
form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Lowercase letters a–z, digits and hyphens, as the Agent Skills format requires. The name of the skill's folder.
form.description: What it does and when to use it
form.descriptionHint: Up to {{max}} characters. The assistant always sees it, and decides by it whether to load the skill.

skippedReason.script: a script: this extension runs no code
skippedReason.many: over the limit of 50 files or 1 MB

errors.header: This is not a skill: a SKILL.md starts with a header (name, description) between two lines of "---".
errors.builtinName: A built-in skill has this name. Choose another.
errors.taken: A skill with this name is installed already.
errors.description: Say what it does and when to use it.
errors.descriptionLong: The description is longer than 1024 characters.

errors.tooMany: No more than {{max}} skills can be installed.
errors.address: Enter an address that starts with https://.
errors.fetch: The skill could not be fetched. Download it and use "From a file".

errors.compatibilityLong: The compatibility field is longer than 500 characters.

errors.archive: The zip file could not be read.

errors.name: The skill needs a name.
